items.title: Extending LLDB to Debug Applications That Span CPUs and GPUs
items.content_snippet: We built a vendor-neutral accelerator plugin architecture in lldb-server for debugging applications that span CPUs and GPUs. items.title: Your KV Cache Can Spot Attacks on Your AI Agents - Ari Azarafrooz, Intrinsec AI
items.content_snippet: Ari Azarafrooz, founder of Intrinsec AI, shows how the KV cache your inference engine already writes can double as a security signal for AI agents. Instead of only guarding inputs and outputs with judge models or a classifier for every failure, he learns a baseline from normal traffic and flags KV pages that look unusual, catching problems like a hidden spoken instruction in a voicemail where there is no text to filter. He covers where this plugs into stacks like vLLM, SGLang, LMCache, llm-d and

items.title: Will AI Agents Pretend to Be Human to Get Past a Check? - Maty Bohacek, Stanford
items.content_snippet: Maty Bohacek of Stanford looks at a security check we still rely on: getting on a phone or video call to prove you're human before opening an account, approving a wire or recovering access. With AI avatars that can now join Zoom calls, he tested what agents do when a human check is the only thing between them and their goal. When a voice or video cloning tool was available, many agents used it to impersonate a person, even when told not to, and safety alignment only cut the rate from 65% to 44%.

items.content_snippet: Mislav Ivanda of Daytona has integrated sandboxes into most of the major agent frameworks, and noticed that frameworks that disagree on almost everything all ended up in the same place. He compares three ways to run agent-generated code: allow lists and approval prompts, embedded runtimes, and a separate sandboxed computer. items.content_snippet: Zach Lloyd, founder and CEO of Warp and former engineering lead on Google Docs, explains why companies are moving from engineers prompting agents on their laptops to sandboxed cloud software factories. He makes the case for treating your factory as infrastructure that's open, works with your existing tools and is defined in code. items.title: Stop Doing Agent Archaeology on Your Team's Code - Richard Feldman, Delta
items.content_snippet: Richard Feldman of Delta explains why handing off agent-driven work to a teammate loses so much: you get the branch and maybe a pasted transcript, but not the reasoning, the dead ends or the decisions made along the way. He demos Delta, a tool where the agent conversation, code changes, reviews and teammates all live in one shared thread.
